description_full: Camtek Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, develops, manufactures, and sells inspection and metrology equipment for semiconductor industry in the United States, China, Korea, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. The company offers Hawk, a platform engineered for advanced packaging; Eagle G5 for enhanced detection and metrology; Eagle-i/Plus, a system that delivers 2D inspection and metrology capabilities; Eagle-AP/Plus, which addresses the advanced packaging market using software and hardware technologies that deliver 2D and 3D inspection and metrology capabilities on the same platform; and Golden Eagle for the inspection and metrology of standard panel sizes. It also develops MicroProf AP, a wafer metrology tool for applications at 3D packaging process steps; MicroProf DI, an optical inspection tool that enables inspection of structured and unstructured wafers; MicroProf FE, a 2D/3D wafer metrology tool; MicroProf FS, a wafer metrology tool configurable; MicroProf PT for hybrid metrology applications to common panel sizes; MicroProf MHU metrology tool, a material handling unit for the semiconductor, MEMS, sapphire, and LED industries; MicroProf TL, an optical surface measurement tool for fully automatic 3D surface measurements; MicroProf 200, a measuring device for contactless and non-destructive characterization of surfaces and films; and MicroProf 300, a SurfaceSens technology for quality assurance, development, and manufacturing. The company serves semiconductor manufacturers, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test, integrated device manufacturers, and wafer level packaging subcontractors. Camtek Ltd. was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Migdal HaEmek, Israel.
ceo_bio: Mr. Rafi  Amit | CEO & Director | Age 76 | Compensation: $1.1M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 709 people. Revenue per employee of $700K ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers, improving at 12%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $180K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $24K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: Camtek Ltd. is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.5B market cap on $496M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +17% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 33% against a 12% cost of capital — a 21-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 47%.

The business throws off $127M in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.80× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin -233.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 37% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 26% operating margin runs 19pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.10x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+21.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 29% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 39% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 55% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 72% and a beta of 1.43, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.33 vs 5y 1.77), so read it loosely.
About $55.6M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 52% in the 2020 crash, 56% in the 2022 bear market and 86% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $58.42 (margin of safety -66%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 44%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $36.41 to $97.92 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 36.5 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 29.4 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 35.6 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 12% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $167 on average, 72% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 33% clears the cost of capital of 11.8% by 21pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.10).
It runs a 47% gross margin and converts 26% of revenue into free cash flow, or 22% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.80x.
ROE of 8% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 9pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 9.7% of revenue on R&D and 3.4% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The company holds more cash than debt.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.1, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 183 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 15.6% over 3 years, 26.1% over 5 years and 17.5% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 22%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 40.4% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.2x, 2.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own 37.4%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 53%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (13 sales, net $5.1M sold).
The share count has grown 1.2% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
Short interest is elevated at 11.4% of the float, 6.8 days to cover.
people: With about 709 employees, each generates about $700K of revenue, 1.9x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 11.6% a year.
That works out to $180K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.1M (2x revenue per employee).
